sentences.text: Mcnamaraspis is sometimes called "The Gogo Fish" because its holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was excavated from the Gogo Formation.
Mcnamaraspis kaprios was a marine fish that grew to a maximum length of 0.5 meters.
The animal possessed a distinct cartilaginous snout that has not been recorded in other placoderms.
Mcnamaraspis kaprios was proclaimed the first official state fossil emblem of any Australian state on December 5, 1995.
John A. Long discovered and described the type specimen of Mcnamaraspis in the Gogo Formation near Fitzroy Crossing.
Mcnamaraspis is inferred to have been an active predator that used its sharp, razor-like teeth to crack the shells of arthropods like trilobites.
Mcnamaraspis belongs to the class Placodermi.
It is classified within the superfamily Incisoscutoidea, the clade Coccosteomorphi, and the larger clade Eubrachythoraci.
Mcnamaraspis lived in ancient reef systems in northwestern Australia during the Frasnian epoch of the Late Devonian, approximately 380 to 375 million years ago.
The fossil record for Mcnamaraspis spans from 382.31 to 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
